title: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates
description: Convert your hourly rate to an annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Compare the National Minimum Wage with award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, annual salary is hourly rate × 38 × 52; the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour gives $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full‑time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax, super, and any deductions. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44/hour from 1 July 2026) is the base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations, and they include penalty rates, allowances, and classification structures. Most employees are covered by an award, so their minimum pay is likely above the National Minimum Wage. Check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your award.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied and does it affect my salary conversion?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05/hour. When converting to an annual salary, you can calculate the gross annual amount including loading by using the loaded hourly rate in the formula. However, remember that super is still paid on top of the loaded rate, and your actual take‑home pay will depend on tax and Medicare.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Salary from an Hourly Rate

Whether you are negotiating a job offer, comparing roles, or planning your budget, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual salary ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a full‑time week of 38 ordinary hours, which is the benchmark used by the Fair Work Commission and the Fair Work Ombudsman. If your actual hours differ, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. The result is your gross annual salary before tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for employees in the national system who are not covered by an award or registered agreement. Using the formula:

- $26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,254.80 per year**

However, most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services (SCHADS) Award have recently updated their pay rates. Award rates include classification structures, penalty rates, and allowances that can significantly increase your salary. Always check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman to find your correct minimum rate.

### Casual Loading and Its Effect on Salary

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (such as annual leave and sick leave). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. If you are a casual worker, your annual salary calculation should use the loaded rate:

- $33.05 × 38 × 52 = **$65,306.80 per year**

Remember, the loading is added to the base rate – never type a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator that adds it again. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to handle this correctly.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Check

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly salary, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the National Minimum Wage example:

- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

This can help you match your pay slip and budget more easily.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund – and this is paid **on top** of your salary, not deducted from it. For the 2026–27 year, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So if your annual salary is $52,254.80, the super contribution would be:

- $52,254.80 × 12% = **$6,270.58 per year**

Your total remuneration (salary plus super) is therefore $58,525.38. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax and Medicare: What You Take Home

Your take‑home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax‑free threshold is $18,200. The rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (the single reduction thresholds used here are from 2025–26 as the 2026–27 figures were not confirmed). For a salary of $52,254.80, the estimated tax would be approximately $7,477, and Medicare $1,045, leaving a take‑home of about $43,733 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

### Average Earnings: A Point of Comparison

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that in May 2026, full‑time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70, which equates to an annual salary of about $108,352.40. All employees (including part‑time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118.40 per year. These figures are higher than the National Minimum Wage because they reflect the mix of occupations and experience across the workforce.

### Key Points to Remember

- The formula **hourly × hours per week × 52** gives your gross annual salary.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour ($33.05 casual) – but most roles are covered by an award with higher rates.
- Super is paid on top at 12% up to the maximum contribution base.
- Tax and Medicare are deducted from your salary, not from super.
- Always check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

For more detailed conversion tools and reference tables, visit our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page or the [reference tables](/data). If you need to check the minimum wage for your age or disability, see the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
